translations.text: Just as, again, I did not tell you who
they are, or what all the other things written in all the letters are.
And perhaps this is the likeness of those chains of darkness in which God bound the angels who abandoned their authority and cast them down into Hades, having revealed himself
with belts and bands bound around him, or loaded onto him with bonds and destruction like that inflicted on Sodom and Gomorrah.
And perhaps this, too, is the meaning of what he said: “I will stretch out my foot over Idumea.” He appeared with belts and bands, trampling on them.
That is why I told you, brothers and sisters, in the house of God, before the altar, on the day when we did bitter things,
Stop your weeping! Stop! Whether you have wept or have not wept, the sword has already become drunk in heaven. It is strong and stretched out in the hands
of the one who handed it over to him, ready to crush. It will return and come upon Idumea, about which I spoke to you in another letter.
But those who lived in it did not believe until the sword came and destroyed them, because they did not take warning when they heard the sound of the trumpet, just as the prophet
say it, nor did they believe the one who first told them
“Do not let those who live in Judea rejoice.”
For the one whose identity they do not know is looking into the distance, ready to stamp his foot upon those in Idumea and those who deceive within it through impure pleasures.
Does every person [?]?
[?] like the one about whom it was said, “For honey drips from the lips of a prostitute, but afterward you will find her more bitter than wormwood.”
Was it not because of those who perished from that disease, or whom that disease afflicted, that anguish weighed upon the prophets from the beginning like a stone?
as they said, “They tormented my life in a pit; they placed a stone upon me. Waters poured over my head. I said, ‘He has abandoned me.’”
He did not, then, abandon him, as it is said: “I cried out to your name, Lord, from a deep pit. You heard my voice.”
Do not close your ears to my plea. You came near to help me on the day when I called upon you. You told me, ‘Do not be afraid.’ You pleaded the cases of my soul, Lord; you redeemed my life.
You saw my troubles, Lord, for you saw them, and I did not hide them from you. You judged my case.”

Nor, for its part, does what they say about those wasting away in this wasting disease mean that it was their own will that took hold of them, to intensify it or not intensify it within them until it gained strength in their bodies.
They said, “You will repay them, Lord, according to the works of their hands.
You will repay them with suffering according to the strength of their hearts.
You will pursue them in your anger and destroy them from beneath heaven, Lord.”
Or are the prophets speaking about an actual stone when they say that it was placed on them?

Or are they not saying this because of the sickness of anguish in which they find themselves, or which is within them and has weighed upon them like a stone, because of those whom they see stricken with that pestilential disease?
And they also said, “They placed a stone on me,” because of the blows dealt to those people, which torment their souls to the point of death.
For they were killed.
How can anyone say that the prophets do not share in the anguish that rests upon them because of those who are wasting away, or who waste away at any time, in this disease,
since they themselves foresee both what is happening and what will happen?

Not only do they see from afar what will happen to people on earth before it happens, but they have also foreseen, or understood, what will happen to sinners on the day of wrath, and what will happen to the righteous,
just as the one who speaks in them, who is God, says: “My servants will eat. My servants will drink. My servants will rejoice. My servants will exult with gladness.
But you will hunger. But you will thirst. But you will be put to shame. But you will shriek because of the anguish of your hearts, and you will cry out because your spirits are broken.”
Whom is he addressing as “you,” except those who will die wasting away in that pestilential disease?
So, concerning these two kinds of suffering—that of punishment and that of all who are tormented by that evil disease—the suffering of punishments, or of hell, will hold them for a time to come.
of everyone who dies persisting in it, or with it persisting in them—that the prophets said in the suffering of their anguish: “My heart is broken within me; they trembled,
all my bones. I became like a broken man, and like a man overcome by wine, before the Lord and before the greatness of the beauty of his glory.
“For the earth is full of adultery. The earth mourned in the face of these things.”
Just as he also says, “I trembled at the destruction of the daughter of my people.”
“Suddenly pains overcame me, like those of a woman about to give birth.”
Or again, “My heart, my heart causes me anguish.”

Not only did the prophets and all the righteous suffer anguish, sorrow, and groaning, or suffer the pain of anguish because of those suffering from the whole disease of lawlessness, but the Savior too,

When the Lord of all became human for the salvation of humanity, he himself also suffered, just as all the righteous suffered anguish because of our sins, through the disease that came upon all of us.
But it was all our diseases, or the evils that came upon us, that he drew upon himself, as Scripture testifies: “He is the one who bore our sins.”
and all our afflictions,” so that sin might not rule from that moment onward over those who would be freed from the disease of every kind of lawlessness. And as for those who have not been freed
through the disease of sin, he will bring their sins, which he drew upon himself or bore, back upon them once again, because they did not remember how they placed a crown of thorns
on his head. Nor did they remember that the prophets, the apostles, and all the righteous endured agonies, or fell into agonies, because of our sins.

If someone wants to rescue people from great affliction and save them from deep anguish, and those people in turn hide themselves from him in his affliction and anguish, they themselves know that they are rejoicing.
O you alone, God, whose works are all truth and righteous judgments, who know the distress of this sickness that has put my poverty to the test!
For I recognized my sins through your teaching, or through your instructing me.

My heart and [?] are full of fire, or have been set on fire by the burning that penetrates them through the heat of that evil disease, which burns in my two [?], this one and that one, and my knees, and also my feet.

For this reason I cannot refrain from saying this other bitter, or immoderate, thing: not only will I celebrate this Passover with you, or among you, as a stranger, but I will also spend the remaining days
of my life, all of them, taking care of my life as a stranger, as I have already said in other letters written to all of you concerning those who do, or who have now done,
these pestilential and abominable deeds among you, whether male or female—and not because of you yourselves, the holy brothers and sisters among you, whether male or female, whether old or young.
For just as judgment, bloodguilt, and still greater miseries fall upon the one speaking with you if he makes himself a stranger to you yourselves,
my beloved, so too judgment and bloodguilt fall upon him if he maintains a friendship with those who practice, or will practice, pestilent deeds among you.
Instead, their judgment and their bloodguilt fall upon themselves because of the resolve of the one who does not agree with them.

Therefore, whether he confronts this sickness or does not confront it, so that its stench does not rise or spread abroad, but remains concealed, or is covered over, until the last of its foul stench settles

on his clothing; and even if he gathers together with the whole congregation in every matter, in every way, according to every ordinance of God, being an enemy of those who have not obeyed or will not obey,
the words and commandments that God commanded in his congregations, so as not to let a person who has that disease upon him scratch himself, in order that they may find relief or be healed of it.

yet they have also rubbed him among them with many kinds of rubbing, laughing, and have rubbed themselves along with him through his activity, which is powerful in rubbing [?], until his wounds multiply,
They did not fear God. They felt no shame before people. They had no pity on themselves.
Nor did they think that their sins would return upon their heads, and their acts of ungodliness upon the tops of their heads.
Did they not also know that the distress and sorrow of the one who turns his heart toward estrangement from them, or toward hostility, would return and fall upon them?

because they did not believe what he said in other letters, in which the written word of God says this: “Who will alienate a holy place from God through his pestilent deeds?” Just as he says, “You have made this place foreign to me.”
And that God should not make those people strangers to himself, whether male or female, who commit or will commit abominations at any time within his congregations.

This favor is not due to you, you deceitful people—that God has not withdrawn from his holy places because of your abominable deeds. Rather, it is due to his mercies and to the faithful brothers who live among you.
If people make room for estrangement from God through their impiety, people also make room for God to draw near to them through their righteous deeds, and for God to bring them near to himself.

For refrain from letting this man, whose identity you do not know, take some of his hidden things, which you do not know or understand, and attach them to things that are not manifest. These are like blood
that has been poured upon blood and, after they have mingled together, has been lifted up and sprinkled down from above upon the heads of these people and into the midst of the congregation.
of those others who commit, or will commit, abominable deeds in his synagogues at all times, with the words that the Lord spoke to his disciples having been fulfilled
upon the unclean men and unclean women who are, or will be, among you: “Shake off the dust of your feet against them as a testimony against them.”
And because they are children of hostility and are not children of peace.
For peace and those who have been made masters of peace know who is worthy for their peace to rest [?] upon them [?].
Who are the unworthy, upon whom it should not rest, but from whom peace should return to itself, or to the places it knows, which it makes its resting places,
resting upon them, fulfilling or taking the place of the Lord’s disciples at all times, until the end of the age, just as he commanded them:
“As for the children of peace, let your peace rest upon them. As for the children of hostility, let your peace turn away from them and return to you.”
Or is peace not the companion of the righteous?
And is the spirit of the righteous not the companion of peace?
And those with whom peace will dwell will become sons of peace and daughters of blessing.
And those against whom Peace will be hostile will become sons of hostility and sons of the curse.
Oh, woe to you, those who have destroyed their virginity and their worth among you, and have defiled their endurance or the works of their endurance!
Your killers are not human killers. Rather, they are killers arising from your very selves.
That boar and that sow [?], about whom they spoke [?] in Scripture, are the ones who have destroyed your soul and gnawed it with their teeth and tusks.
The congregations have become filled with groaning, weeping, and cries: “Oh, oh! How long will they go on committing these abominations in God’s holy places?”
And: “Do not do these pestilential deeds.”
Utterly and completely. And yet you did not listen until your heart died [?] Hades [?] or this sickness [?] evil [?] truly [?] prick it [?] its stings with the itching that is sweet for the moment.
For you have not blunted its sting or its stings, you false virgins, whether male or female, among you—those who will commit abominations within the congregations at any time.
What will you say before those who tormented death and conquered death by striking it with their virginity or their widowhood, and destroying its sting—or its sting
was destroyed before them through their true righteousness—when death has tormented you by conquering you through its defilements, its impurities, its thefts, and its other pestilential deeds?
—or will the one who remembers the evil deeds you have done not vomit bile and become like those who vomit?
How will you taunt death, saying, “Death, where is your victory? Hades, where is your sting?” when it has destroyed your hope, or you have destroyed it through death by your evil deeds?
You yourselves bear witness against yourselves through them, as to what sort of things, or what things, you have done after all those commands from God.

You boast [?] instead [?] because [?] which you [?] it [?] you [?] to it, “Death, where is your victory?” Rather, where is your victory? Or, “Hades, where is your sting?” As though truly [?]—rather, where is your strength?
which he destroyed,
or which she destroyed through the poison of his sting, which she spread.
Wrath, anger upon anger, curse upon curse, judgment and bloodguilt upon judgment and bloodguilt, upon the heads of those who practice, or will practice, those wicked deeds among you at any time.
Just as, in turn, mercy upon mercy, blessing upon blessing, grace upon grace, power upon strength rest upon the heads of those who practice, or will practice, righteous deeds among you at any time.
Or in what way is this saying, “Repay,” or “Take vengeance,” more excessive than the many such words I have spoken in my anguish?
I said it while you were listening, brothers, in the place where we sat on the mountain outside the meeting place, near the rock or the cliff:
“I have sent for you again today so that you may understand that sorrow is bitter, just as you have seen its bitterness increasing around
the place about which I told you, ‘God did not speak with me,’ so that no one would think anything beyond what he hears me say.
Rather, this is the place where they laid a trap for me while you were letting me come in to you, on the day that I told you which it was, and that there are still millstones on the road to this day.

And in saying this, I said, ‘Just as I have not gathered with you in uprightness or unity of heart to pray or to examine a word of God—look, it has been more than seven months—neither will I gather now.’
And why is that?
Is it not because of this number of people whom God made strangers to us within two months because of those pestilent deeds that we have not stopped doing to this day, whether male or female?
How could they not be bitter?
The sorrow whose bitter deeds testify about it, or mingle with it, is like something sweet with a great deal of bitterness mixed into it, taking away the sweetness within it.
Just as we tore the tunics and ripped off the belts of those who sinned among us, like soldiers, because they had sinned against their king, Jesus,
We pursued them and drove them out from among us, although they were our brothers and sisters, our children, our fellow servants, and our fellow soldiers of the one Lord, God, the King, the Almighty.
Oh, the great sorrow!

For if it is a sorrow that God has thrown out of his congregations those who were caught committing abominations among us, although they will not lack bread and water in whatever place each one wished to go,
then how great will the sorrow be in the place where we will go, when we see those who will die in the deceitful deeds they do secretly in these congregations being thrown
out of the places of rest in the kingdom of heaven into the fire that never goes out, the place where there is neither water nor bread, where there is no relief at all.
Listen to this statement, and let us pay attention to it.
Those who die, or those who will die among us—will we say of them all
that they are righteous, or that they are virgins, or that they have entered into life, or that they have received the crown?
The prophet says, ‘He put on a garment of vengeance’—that is, God—‘and his zeal, like a repayment, will repay retribution to his enemies.’
“And those who hate you, he will repay them.”
The one who dragged Esau down—that is, God—as the prophet says: ‘I myself dragged Esau down. I uncovered the hidden things of their [?].’
hide—he is also the one who drags down, or will drag down, those who commit, or will commit, defilements, impurities, and every deceitful deed among you now, you synagogues.
He uncovered the hidden things that they were unable to hide from God, not from a human being.
Understand what you are saying, you who kill yourselves with the spears of sin, which are all their deceitful deeds:
‘If we were visible to people in our abominable deeds but hidden from God in our wicked deeds, then let each one, every single person, carry out his lawless acts.
For what will they do to me or to you if they discover our evil deeds or learn about them?’

Our sins are hidden from people but visible to God. So in many ways, or in many forms, he will expose the filth, the defilements, and every deceitful deed that we do or will do in these congregations at any time.
Is it not a disgrace and a great [?] for the congregation that our fathers gathered together through hardships?
He was fastened in the stocks by the one who gave them strength, Jesus, if I speak according to what is written.
“That [?].”
